title: Control of goose grass in perennial crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of goose grass in perennial crop fields - Vietnam
Eleusine indica Cỏ mần trầu, ngưu cản

Prevention: Avoid overgrazing – dense grass prevents the weed establishing.
Mulch soil to kill weed seeds down to 5cm.
Only use certified seedlings to avoid introduction through contamination.
Reduce soil compaction by limiting traffic, especially when the soils are wet.
Use intercropping with soybean or sweet potato.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: perennial crops such as citrus, litchi, longan, and mango.
Tufted annual grass, spreading or stands straight, up to 40cm tall.
Leaves bright green, flat or folded along central vein, up to 8mm wide and 15cm long.
Inflorescences with 3-8 'branches', each with two dense rows of flowers.
Inspect fields monthly for the presence of the weed.
The weed spreads along disturbed habitats such as roads and powerline corridors - make a monthly inspection of those areas near your fields.
Also, look for it along marshes and stream banks.
Direct Control: Hand-pull or remove by hoeing, best before flowering, and then remove tubers from the soil.
Removal gets harder as the root system gets stronger.
Use mulching materials such as soybean, sweet potato, rice, water hyacinth residues to suppress the weed.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Seedlings up to the four-leaf stage can be controlled by glyphosate (1900-2000g a.i/ha).
Eleusine indica is susceptible to virtually all groups of standard grass-killing herbicides.
